name: the two of us

1.definition: Identifies a group while explicitly giving its size.
1.details: The four of us can describe the group of four that includes the speaker. If a larger group is salient, the phrase needs a recoverable set of four. Without the, four of us can simply pick an unspecified subset of a larger us-group. The scope of the definite is the group picked out by the whole NP.

examples.form: There were six of us, and [four of us] had bikes.
examples.note: Constructed subset with the article absent.

examples.form: I was there with Jo, Lee and Pat. [The four of us] shared a tent.
examples.note: Constructed definite whose numeral matches the contextually salient group.

relatedConstructions.notes: The article determines the whole NP.
Cardinals with of-phrases can occur in ordinary partitive syntax.

grounds.note: Lists several cardinals and personal pronouns with the group-size function.
Notes the standard cardinal and the less widely accepted both variant.

projection.target: A cardinal with the can count members of an already identified group. Without the, the same numeral and pronoun also admit an unspecified subset of a larger salient group.
projection.evidence: CASA records the cardinal and pronoun slots and the group-size reading. CGEL explicitly contrasts the two of us with both of us and dialectal the both of us.

curious.title: The two of us, the four of us
curious.summary: The, a number and of plus a pronoun together name a group and say how many are in it.
curious.body: I was there with Jo, Lee and Pat. The four of us shared a tent. The phrase the four of us can point to a group of four that includes the speaker, and it gives the group's size at the same time. When a larger group is also in the picture, the phrase needs a set of four the listener can pick out. Without the, it works differently. In There were six of us, and four of us had bikes, four of us picks out some of a larger group rather than naming the whole group. This dictionary treats the analysis as provisional.

examples.text: I was there with Jo, Lee and Pat. [The four of us] shared a tent.
There were six of us, and [four of us] had bikes.

curious.try: Think of a group you were part of. How would you name it with the, a number and of us? What if only some of the group did something?

teacher.summary: Helps explain the four of us (a recoverable group of four) versus four of us (an unspecified subset of a larger group).
teacher.explain: The pattern is NP[the + cardinal + of + personal pronoun], as in the four of us. It identifies a group while explicitly giving its size, and the article determines the whole NP. The numeral must match a contextually recoverable group, so the four of us can describe the group of four that includes the speaker. Without the, four of us can simply pick an unspecified subset of a larger us-group. Cardinals with of-phrases can also occur in ordinary partitive syntax. The analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: The is a determinative (often called the definite article).

examples.text: I was there with Jo, Lee and Pat. [The four of us] shared a tent.
There were six of us, and [four of us] had bikes.

contrasts.text: The four of us shared a tent.
contrasts.note: Definite; the numeral matches the contextually salient group.
No the; can pick an unspecified subset of a larger group.

watch_for: A learner might read four of us, without the, as naming a whole group of four, when it can pick an unspecified subset of a larger group.
A learner might use the two of us for a pair that isn't the contextually identified group.
teacher.activity: Describe a picture of a group of six, with three friends sitting together. Students write sentences about the whole group and about parts of it, with and without the, and say which group each sentence names.

child.hook: What can you call a group of friends and say how many without naming each one?
child.explain: You can name a group by saying the, a number and of us. The four of us shared a tent. It points to a group of four that you can pick out from the situation.

examples.text: [The four of us] shared a tent.

child.play: Pick a group you were in, like a team or a table at lunch. Say how many were in it using the number and of us. Then say what some of the group did.
